label: rem1.2
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem1.2}
\textnormal{Let $s\ge 0$ and $0<b<2$. Assume that $0<\sigma \le \frac{4-2b}{n-2s} $, if $s<\frac{n}{2} $, and that $0<\sigma <\infty $, if $s\ge \frac{n}{2} $. If $\sigma $ is not an even integer, assume further $\left\lceil s\right\rceil \le\sigma +1$. Then we can easily verify that $f\left(u\right)=\lambda \left|u\right|^{\sigma } u$ with $\lambda \in \mathbb C$ is a model case of class $X\left(\sigma,s,b\right)$. See also \cite{DYC13,W04,WHHG11} for example.}

label: thm 1.3.

label: cor 1.4.
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor 1.4.}
Let $n\in \mathbb N$, $0<s<1$, $0<b<\hat{2}$ and $\sigma _{0} <\sigma <\sigma _{s} $. Assume that $f\left(u\right)=\lambda \left|u\right|^{\sigma } u$ with $\lambda \in \mathbb C$. Then there exists a corresponding $\delta >0$ such that for any $u_{0} \in H^{s} (\mathbb R^{n})$ satisfying $\left\| u_{0} \right\| _{H^{s} (\mathbb R^{n})} \le \delta $, $(1.1)$ has a unique global solution satisfying $(1.8)$.
head: environment

label: cor 1.5.
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor 1.5.}
Let $n\ge 2$, $s=1$, $0<b<\hat{2}$ and $\sigma _{0} <\sigma <\sigma _{s} $. Assume that $f\left(u\right)=\lambda \left|u\right|^{\sigma } u$ with $\lambda \in \mathbb C$. Then there exists a corresponding $\delta >0$ such that for any $u_{0} \in H^{1} (\mathbb R^{n})$ satisfying $\left\| u_{0} \right\| _{H^{1} (\mathbb R^{n})} \le \delta $, $(1.1)$ has a unique global solution satisfying $(1.8)$.
head: environment

label: rem 1.6
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem 1.6}
\textnormal{Corollary 1.5 and Corollary 1.6 improve the global well--poseness result of \cite{G17}. First, Guzm\'{a}n \cite{G17} didn't treat the case $\frac{1}{2}<s<1$ for $n=1$, while Corollary 1.5 holds for any $n\in \mathbb N$ and $0<s<1$. Next, we can easily see that $\tilde{2}<\hat{2}$ for $n\le 3$ and $0<s\le \min \left\{1,\;\frac{n}{2} \right\}$.}

label: lem 2.1.

body_md:
\label{lem 2.1.}
Let $s>0$, $1<p<\infty $ and $v=s-\left[s\right]$. Then $\sum _{\left|\alpha \right|=\left[s\right]}\left\|D^{\alpha }f\right\| _{\dot{H}_{p}^{v}}  $ is an equivalent norm on $\dot{H}_{p}^{s} (\mathbb R^{n})$.

label: rem 3.2.

body_md:
\label{rem 3.2.}
\textnormal{Lemma 3.1 generalizes Lemma 3.3 of \cite{AK21} and Lemma 2.1 of \cite{W04}. In fact, Lemma 3.3 of \cite{AK21} follows directly from Lemma 3.1 by putting $\delta=0$, $s_{0}=s$. Lemma 2.1 of \cite{W04} also follows directly from Lemma 3.1 by using the embeddings $\dot{B}_{r,2}^{s} \subset \dot{H}_{r}^{s}$, $\dot{H}_{r'}^{s}\subset \dot{B}_{r',2}^{s}$, where $\dot{B}_{p,q}^{s} $ is homogeneous Besov space (see e.g. \cite{WHHG11}).}
